metadata.title: Claude, Reorder Policy.
metadata.subtitle: A Rule, Not a Judgment Call
metadata.purpose: Take a Claude skill apart in the Teardown register: when Claude recommends a reorder, it isn't judging the market — it's running a written list of steps in SKILL.md, and it can't handle a case the list doesn't cover. Name the trade-off: they optimized for repeatability at the expense of coverage.

beats.narration_text: Liam here, in for Bear. You'd guess Claude just knows how much stock to reorder — a judgment call about the market. It doesn't. It follows a written rule. Here's what's actually happening under the hood.

beats.narration_text: Take a Claude skill apart, and here's what you find. It's a folder — Claude reads it before it acts. This one's called reorder-policy. Open it up: one file inside, SKILL.md. Plain language, no hidden logic, no secret sauce.

The reasonable-sounding read: Claude is weighing this the way a person would. Supplier trust. Seasonal demand. Gut feel about the market. Case by case, judgment call. That's the honest guess. It's also wrong.

Open SKILL.md. Nothing weighs anything — no reasoning to reconstruct. What's actually there is a Steps section: a numbered list Claude runs top to bottom. Nowhere on the list does any step say 'use your judgment.'

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the Steps section, no judgment step

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — STEPS
production_viz.caption: the whole method, top to bottom

beats.narration_text: Here's the mechanism, in full. Claude reads each step in order and runs it. No branching — unless a step itself says to branch. Read the step, run the step, next step. That's it.

Feed identical stock numbers in twice, and the steps hand back the identical recommendation both times. That repeatability is real — it's what they optimized for. Here's what it costs. Ask it something the list doesn't cover, and there's no step left to run. The list only ever does what's written on it.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same Steps list, both directions

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS
production_viz.caption: same numbers twice; an uncovered case gets nothing extra

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill isn't Claude judging the market. It's Claude running a written list of steps, in order — repeatable to a fault, and blind to what the list doesn't cover.

props.quote: A Claude skill isn't Claude judging the market. It's Claude running a written list of steps, in order — repeatable to a fault, and blind to what the list doesn't cover.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: ask it to write a short SKILL.md for a reorder-policy skill, then run it twice on the same numbers, then run it on a case the list doesn't cover. Watch where it stops. Go deeper: add a step that says 'use your judgment,' and see whether the list still behaves like a list — or has just handed the whole decision back to the model.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to understand how Claude runs a written skill. A Claude 'skill' is a folder holding SKILL.md — a numbered list of steps Claude reads and runs top to bottom, with no judgment step. Write me a short SKILL.md for a REORDER-POLICY skill: three to five numbered steps that turn stock-on-hand, weekly demand, and lead-time into a reorder recommendation. Then run it twice on the same numbers and show the output is identical. Then run it on a case the list clearly doesn't cover, and show me exactly where it stops.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: add a sixth step that says 'use your judgment.' Does the list still behave like a list — or has it just handed the whole decision back to the model?
